projects.title: ChatGPT and Claude Context Transfer
projects.summary: I show a practical workflow for moving useful context from Claude to ChatGPT without copying your full chat history. First, I export what Claude knows from memory and past chats, review outdated details, and turn the useful parts into a portable Markdown profile. Then I upload that profile to a new ChatGPT chat, check what it understood, and update the memory I want ChatGPT to keep. The goal is to avoid starting from zero whenever you switch assistants.
projects.summaryZh: 在 ChatGPT 与 Claude 间迁移上下文的工作流：导出 Claude 记忆为 Markdown，上传到 ChatGPT 并更新记忆，避免切换助手时从零开始。

projects.title: Show HN: Windows-style Excel ribbon shortcuts and formatting macros for Mac
projects.author: tjds
projects.summary: I worked in finance for 5+ years and became extremely proficient with Excel on Windows. When I left to build a start-up, I switched to a Mac, and was frustrated by the absence of the shortcuts I had become accustomed to, which is why I built LightningXL on the side. LightningXL is a menu-bar app that uses macOS Accessibility tools to add back two things on Mac that I had on Windows: (1) Access to all the ribbon commands across Excel/PowerPoint/Word using the same shortcuts as on Windows, and (2) formatting / auditing / tracing macro capabilities, similar to Macabacus. None of the existing options provides the same scope of functionality: Accelerator Keys helps with the ribbon shortcuts, but not the macros, and the key tips that Microsoft released in the past year or so don't let you traverse the full ribbon. My Excel efficiency is now close to what it used to be on Windows, so I wanted to share LightningXL more broadly for the other power users out there who for a multitude of reasons are using Macs. Would love feedback on what improvements can be made and what other functionality to add for Excel or the rest of the Office suite.

projects.title: 做了一个浏览器扩展，根据打开的网页提供一些顺手执行的动作……欢迎交流～
projects.author: hqweay
projects.summary: ## TLDR - 一个浏览器插件 - 根据打开的网页提供一些动作，可以实现划词翻译、多选元素截图分享、网页剪藏、简单的自动化等操作 - 这是 AI 生成的 landing page: [顺手 · 会看场合的网页工具]( https://shunshou.leay.net/) - 当然，免费。仓库还没开源，先看看这个思路有没有人感兴趣…… ## 正文 核心是根据打开的网页，把对应能顺手做的事放在旁边。所以引入了一个悬浮可展开的按钮和划词后的气泡。 一些场景示例： 1. 划词翻译 2. 将豆瓣图书、豆瓣电影、B 站视频的元数据保存到笔记软件。 3. 剪藏内容放到笔记软件或保存 markdown 到本地。 4. 任意选择网页上的元素并截图拼接分享。 5. 将 Instagram 、小红书的帖子整合为单图分享…… 6. 简单的自动化：打开豆瓣电影页自动保存元数据到笔记；打开某网站首页自动点击签到…… 7. 搭配组合，能接入 AI 、操作页面，理论上能有一些有趣的玩法。 ![image]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hqweay/picbed/master/img/image-e7t6kdn9lue3n.avif) ![image]( https://shunshou.leay.net/assets/screenshot-selection.png) ![image]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hqweay/picbed/master/img/image-yew6hby6yiwu4.avif) ## 讲讲思路 一如既往的自嗨产物。将整个流程抽象为：连接、提取、能力、配方、场景、模式。越抽象越上头…… 首先把整个网页当作提取信息的上下文，通过点击的方式可视化获取任意 dom ，然后将 dom 转换为我们需要的信息。比如对 dom 进行截图、或者转换为 markdown 文本、获取图片、链接……获取一些结构化的元数据。划选也有语义，于是将划选文本，划选所在的段落都看作可以获取使用的信息。 这些被统一为扩展里的「变量」。 变量之间可以互相组合，搭配 AI ，总之就是获取各种信息。 然后将这些信息再利用扩展提供的「能力」进行一些「动作」。 比如扩展提供了保存文本为文件的能力，搭配变量形成一个动作：提取网页的某个 dom 的文本保存为本地 markdown 文件。 比如扩展提供了保存数据到笔记软件的数据库的能力，搭配提取的变量就可以得到一个书签收集工具。 比如这是一个分享 Instagram 帖子的动作： ![image]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hqweay/picbed/master/img/image-rv6vmc9oh27mx.avif) 这是一个任意选取内容，分享的动作： ![image]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hqweay/picbed/master/img/image-sxqhjgyfk7ewm.avif) ![image]( https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hqweay/picbed/master/img/image-9w7tqdtqr4pzx.avif) 感兴趣的朋友们玩玩！ 可以这里下载：[https://github.com/hqweay/shunshou/releases]( https://github.com/hqweay/shunshou/releases) 欢迎拍砖，欢迎交流～

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Nav Vue，简洁高效的个人网址导航站，基于 Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript 构建。
projects.author: cunyu1943
projects.summary: 简洁高效的个人网址导航站，基于 Vue 3 + Vite + TypeScript 构建。支持站内搜索、多搜索引擎切换，数据完全由 JSON 配置驱动，可一键部署到 GitHub Pages。 特性 📌 固定顶栏：品牌导航栏始终固定在顶部（毛玻璃效果），滚动不消失；滚动离开搜索区后顶栏自动淡入紧凑搜索框（与主页搜索框互斥，不会同时出现），随时发起搜索 🌓 明暗主题：顶栏一键切换黑暗/明亮模式，记忆用户选择，默认跟随系统偏好，刷新无闪烁 🗂️ 分类导航：侧边栏锚点导航（移动端自动切换为横向滑动分类条），分类标题滚动吸顶 📐 规整网格：每行固定 5 个卡片（小屏按断点降级 4/3/2/1 列） 📱 全端自适应：320px 手机到 1920px 桌面均无横向滚动；窄屏按断点收起顶栏品牌名与副标题，优先保证搜索框与卡片的可用宽度 📶 自动折叠：每个分类超过 3 行默认折叠，底部一键展开/收起；搜索过滤时自动全部展开 🔍 站内搜索：输入即过滤，匹配名称 / 描述 / URL / 标签，命中关键词高亮；搜索框尾部为 Google 风格的圆形「清除 + 搜索」按钮（有输入才显示清除） 🌐 多引擎切换：Hero 搜索框与顶栏紧凑搜索框最左侧均内置引擎下拉（图标 + 名称），支持站内、必应、百度、Google、DuckDuckGo、GitHub，默认站内搜索，两处选择实时同步且自动记忆 🛡️ 跳转确认：点击网站卡片先弹窗提示「即将前往【网址】，此链接与本网站无关，请自行判断」，点「继续访问」才在新标签页打开，点「取消跳转」/ Esc / 点遮罩即关闭，避免误点离开本站 🖼️ 灵活 Logo：支持本地目录、在线 URL、自动 favicon 服务三级来源，加载失败自动降级为首字母头像 📦 纯静态：构建产物为纯静态文件，无需后端；数据修改后无需改代码 🚀 自动部署：内置 GitHub Actions 流水线，推送即自动测试 + 构建 + 发布 🪟 全站毛玻璃：全局光斑 + 网格底图打底，顶栏 / 搜索框 / 网站卡片 / 侧边导航 / 吸顶标题 / 跳转确认弹窗统一玻璃质感；模糊半径与透明度集中在 src/styles/main.css 的 --glass- 变量里调节 🎛️ 导航栏可配置：顶栏显示项（logo / 标题 / 副标题 / 紧凑搜索框 / 主题按钮）、高度、是否固定、自定义链接与二级下拉菜单全部由 config.json 的 nav 段驱动；桌面端菜单紧跟在站点 logo 之后，窄屏自动收进汉堡菜单 🔠 悬停小动效：鼠标移到卡片上时，名称与描述若超出一行被截断即左右往返滚动（未超出不滚动），同时 logo 转动一圈；两处动效均遵循系统「减少动态效果」偏好 🎨 图标三选一：顶栏导航链接与分类图标共用同一种写法 —— Iconify 图标名、iconfont 字体图标（可自托管、离线可用）与图片，换图标只改 JSON ✅ 质量保障：vitest 单元测试覆盖搜索、引擎与主题核心逻辑 🛠️ 技术栈 | 类别 | 选型 | | --- | --- | | 框架 | Vue 3（<script setup> 组合式 API） | | 构建 | Vite 7 | | UI / 样式 | Nuxt UI 4（组件 + 语义色体系）+ Tailwind CSS 4 | | 语言 | TypeScript（strict 模式） | | 测试 | Vitest + happy-dom | | 包管理 | pnpm（不锁定版本，≥ 10 即可） | | 部署 | GitHub Pages + GitHub Actions |

projects.title: Show HN: Echodot – Local-first AI that writes replies in your tone
projects.author: kariku
projects.summary: I built echodot – a free, open-source desktop app that drafts replies in your personal writing style. Problem: Most AI writing tools either force you into their voice or require constant copy-pasting between apps. Tools like Cotype are useful but closed-source and cloud-only. What echodot does: - Press a global hotkey (⌘⇧E / Ctrl+Shift+E) - It reads the context (from clipboard) - Generates a reply that matches your tone - Auto-copies the result so you can paste it instantly Key points: - Local-first by default (works with Ollama) - Optional OpenRouter support (bring your own key) - Tone presets + writing samples for better personalization - Streaming responses - Completely free and MIT licensed - No account, no tracking, no subscription Tech stack: Tauri 2 + React + TypeScript + Tailwind Rust backend for hotkeys and system integration GitHub: https://github.com/ohkariku-boop/Echodot Still early (v0.1). Looking for feedback on the core workflow, prompt quality, and what features would make this actually useful day-to-day.

projects.title: [分享创造] 升级 macOS 27 之后菜单栏折叠失效了，所以来推广一下我做的 Knot
projects.author: arjen
projects.summary: 这是一篇推广帖。 升级 macOS 27 后，Knot 原来隐藏菜单栏图片的出了问题，之前用的 [https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden]( https://github.com/dwarvesf/hidden) 也不好用了。于是给 Knot 做了适配。 最初做 Knot 是因为我买了台新 Mac ，常用的功能分散在好几个软件里，所以安装、设置、快捷键都要重新弄，很麻烦。Raycast 的 Quicklinks 自动云同步又需要订阅（所以 Knot 的 Quicklinks 支持导入导出放到 iCloud 上同步），其他很多功能又不到。 常用的功能： - Search：应用、文件搜索和计算器，类似 Raycast 、Alfred 。 - Bar：菜单栏折叠，类似 Hidden Bar 、Ice 。 - Window：窗口分屏，类似 Rectangle 。 - Clipboard：文字、图片剪贴板历史，类似 Maccy 、Raycast 。 - Capture：截图、标注、本地 OCR ，类似 Shottr 、CleanShot X 。（这种一般我都是用微信或者钉钉的） - Quicklinks：关键词打开网址，类似 Raycast Quicklinks 、Alfred 自定义搜索。 另外，macOS 27 的菜单栏适配用到了非公开接口，后续系统更新仍可能影响兼容性，不能保证所有环境都正常。不过有问题我会及时更新推送 MIT 开源，无需账号，没有广告和统计，支持 macOS 14+。 [https://github.com/baomi-app/knot]( https://github.com/baomi-app/knot)

projects.title: Show HN: OpenDocBot – bring your own model to Word, Excel and PowerPoint
projects.author: dgf18
projects.summary: I got tired of the lock-in and black-box nature of AI inside MS Office. One vendor decides which models you can use, where your document data goes, and what the agent is actually allowed to do. And when it fails, you can't see the code or send a PR to add a feature you may need. Many people don't have that choice: they're forced to use these tools (MS Office) at work. For coding agents we already have open interfaces like OpenCode where you can bring your own key, swap providers and models, run local, inspect everything, etc. I thought "agentic Office" needs the same. So I built OpenDocBot: an agent that runs inside Word, Excel and PowerPoint. Bring your own provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, DeepSeek, OpenRouter, Ollama, or your own endpoint / custom gateway). It's client-side, so document data goes straight to the provider you configure, and the source is public so you can always audit the code and self-host it. I added a few things I thought would be useful: human-in-the-loop approval before any action is applied; file uploads (e.g. building a slide deck from a PDF) with local OCR for scanned documents, and tunable model behavior. Caveat: it's early, and Microsoft Marketplace distribution isn't live yet, so today you have to sideload it. I know that's real friction, I'm fighting daily with the MS Support team to achieve MS Partner Center account validation. I wrote some scripts that automate the sideloading process, and recorded short videos to make it easier. If you use Office heavily, I'd love your feedback. Repo: https://github.com/opendocbot/opendocbot Site + docs: https://opendocbot.com

projects.title: Show HN: unSnag – Display tasks you can do and graph task dependencies
projects.author: hydropax
projects.summary: My garage has needed clearing out for quite a while, and to most people it looks like I've just been putting it off. But I'm not procrastinating; the truth is that I'm blocked from doing most of the work. There are two different people that need to remove some heavy equipment that's stored there. Until that's done, I can't access the mess behind the equipment. Since most of my garage clean-up tasks are downstream from the equipment removal, if I focus on those tasks, I feel frustrated because I just can't make progress on that myself. The solution to the frustration is to focus on the things that I actually can do: the things that aren't blocked by other tasks that need to get done first. I think in visual terms, so I built a task/project manager called unSnag ( https://unsnag.app ) that creates a graph showing what tasks you can do right now and what tasks are blocked by prerequisite tasks. You can add your task info manually, or you can have unSnag do it automatically. You can type or dictate all the tasks that are on your mind, how long they'll take, relative importance, due dates, how the tasks relate to other things on your plate, etc. It doesn't need to be in a clean, structured format. You can type or dictate it as a messy "brain dump" in your own language and unSnag will analyze it (currently using OpenAI models) and create the task entries. A deterministic engine then shows you a graph of your tasks, how they relate to each other, which tasks can be worked on right now ("ready"), what your critical paths are to meet your deadlines, and other helpful info. unSnag is free to use, and there's no account needed. The task data lives in your browser and you can export your tasks to a local JSON to back them up, or if you want to sync your tasks across devices via the cloud, you can sign in with Google or using your email address. Couple of honest caveats: This is a web app that looks best on a bigger screen. It'll work on your phone, but the graph view will need to be zoomed and panned because of the small screen. There's no sharing or collaboration. And (for now) it doesn't sync with your calendar or other to-do apps. I'm continuing to build out features, but I'd love your feedback and suggestions. You can leave it here or use the Feedback option in the app. All feedback is welcome, including "I'd never use this"; if that's you, I would appreciate some suggestions for improvement.

projects.title: Show HN: Pelmet – menu bar manager for macOS 27 that hides icons on demand
projects.author: fif7y
projects.summary: Hey, super happy to share about Pelmet, a macOS menu bar manager. It started as a side project during macOS 27 beta and just passed over 500 stars on GitHub and 5000+ downloads in a few weeks. This is crazy to me! Since macOS completely changed the menubar architecture in macOS 27 the tools I was using were no longer working at the time, so I decided to build my own. Hadn't build an app in over a decade and things have changed so much since. I'm a design director so of course special attention went in the user experience and aesthetics (Settings with previews, subtle reveal animations, drag&drop and much more) So macOS now knows how to hide icons natively, it does it when a Mac is locked down for an exam for example, Pelmet reuses the hiding part which then lets macOS know which icons should stay visible. The app does call on a private framework (MenuBarClientCore) resolved at runtime and has a safety net in case it fails, it reports hiding is unavailable instead of breaking the bar. Everything else (positions, clicks, previews, etc.) uses public APIs (Accessibility, ScreenCaptureKit). I'm amazed with the reception Pelmet got, seems I wasn't alone to want a simple menu bar tool that does one thing, and (hopefully) does it well ;) Pelmet was built in native Swift, requires no accounts, no analytics, it's just private. Only external call it does is Sparkle for its updates. The project is free and open source (GPLv3) and hopefully makes many people happy. Get the calm back in your menu bar and happy to answer questions

projects.title: Show HN: FainLane – Paste screenshots into remote coding agents with Ctrl+V
projects.author: primaprashant
projects.summary: Hi all, I run all my CLI coding agents in a remote cloud VM and not being able to paste screenshots has been my only annoyance. So I built this small (2mb) native macOS app that helps me paste screenshots into remote coding agents with Ctrl+V, same as pasting images on coding agents running on my local mac. The app automatically detects the remote host based on the focused window and uploads the image over SSH inside the `~/.cache/fainlane/uploads/` directory on the remote machine and then inserts the path at cursor. The app supports Ghostty, iTerm2, and Apple Terminal. Works even if you have multiple remote hosts you connect to. And works if you use tmux as well.

projects.title: Show HN: Tray indicator for WSL2: on/off, CPU and memory, one-click shutdown
projects.author: bpacholek
projects.summary: When using my PC for private stuff like gaming or video editing I wanted an direct way (without calling wsl --shutdown) of turning WSL2 off. Created (with a help of Claude, it is 2026...) a small tray tool which barely uses resources and provides also resources usage info. Grey means the VM is off. Green, orange or red means it is running, coloured by the higher of its CPU and memory share of the machine. Hover for the numbers, menu entry to shut it down. Two things that were not obvious: * Presence is the vmmemWSL process existing. WSL reports on distributions, not on the VM. * CPU and memory come from NtQuerySystemInformation(SystemProcessInformation). vmmemWSL runs as SYSTEM, so OpenProcess is denied to a normal user and GetProcessTimes is out. A snapshot of ~250 processes takes 3.8 ms and needs no handle. Rust, windows-sys only. 282 KB exe, 3.9 MB private memory after half an hour, one thread while idle. Working set is 10 to 19 MB, mostly shared DLLs. Targeted for Windows 11. Older Win10 builds call it vmmem (Use -process flag). Shutdown asks for confirmation. BSD 3-Clause.

projects.title: Show HN: Omni – Open-source workplace agent, built on Postgres
projects.author: prvnsmpth
projects.summary: Hi HN! Over the past year, I've been building Omni ( https://github.com/getomnico/omni ) - an open-source, self-hosted agent that connects to your workplace apps (drive, email, wiki, CRMs, ticketing systems, etc.), and gives your team an AI agent that can operate across these apps. I posted about Omni on HN about 6 months ago, and it generated some interesting discussions: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=47215427 . At the time, Omni was largely an enterprise search system. Since then, the project has evolved to become more of an agent that can gather context, analyze information, and carry out tasks; rather than just search for answers. E.g., you can tell Omni, "create a project status deck on Google Slides with this week's progress", and it will search through Jira, Slack, Docs, meeting transcripts, fetch the relevant information, analyze spreadsheets with Python, prepare a summary and ask for your approval before creating the slides on your drive. A non-exhaustive list of things Omni can do today: - Take action on connected apps, with an approval system for write actions - Full MCP support, so connectors can integrate with any existing MCP servers. - Sync data from connected apps into a unified search index, allowing the agent to query data across all apps using a single search tool. - Sand-boxed code execution and shell access, enabling the agent to create documents, spreadsheets, presentations and HTML landing pages. - Persistent memory and user-defined skills Omni still uses Postgres as its core data layer where it syncs and indexes all data from connected apps. We use ParadeDB (Postgres extension) for BM25 search and pgvector for semantic search - so there's no need to run and operate a dedicated search cluster or vector database. To know more about the architecture: https://docs.getomni.co/architecture . Would love to get more folks involved in the project, so if you find this interesting, please check out the repo below. It only takes around 10-15 min to deploy using docker compose and connect a few apps. Happy to answer any questions! GitHub: https://github.com/getomnico/omni (Apache 2.0 licensed) Docs: https://docs.getomni.co

github.description: Claude Code & Codex session status and AI usage quotas in your MacBook notch. 把 Claude Code / Codex 会话状态和各家 AI 配额（Claude、Codex、Cursor、Kimi、GLM…）放进刘海。SwiftUI + AppKit，零依赖。

projects.summary: 同时开着几个 Claude Code / Codex 会话时，得不停切窗口看谁在等审批、谁跑完了，配额快见底了也不知道。Tally 是一个 macOS 原生小工具，把这些放进 MacBook 的刘海里：平时和刘海融为一体，有会话等你或跑完了才往下垂一条提示；鼠标停上去展开成面板。 会话按「等你 / 在跑 / 最近」分组；等审批、等输入、跑完了，刘海垂一条提示并响一声。按 Esc 打断、API 报错、主回合结束后子 agent 还在后台跑，这些 hook 不上报的情况也判得准。 点一行跳回那个会话所在的终端标签（Ghostty、Terminal、iTerm2，tmux 的 pane 也行），关掉的会话一键接着聊。 各家配额摆一排：Claude、Codex、Cursor、Antigravity，加上 DeepSeek、Kimi、智谱 GLM、New API 中转站余额；Claude 和 Codex 有今日 / 本周花费和配速线，过 80% 和用完都会提醒。 顺带网速与代理、内存电池、在跑的 app、文件架、合盖不休眠，和一只跟着 CPU 忙闲变化的菜单栏小恐龙。 SwiftUI + AppKit，零第三方依赖；只读各家登录留下的 token，不刷新、不写钥匙串，没有统计上报。要求 macOS 15+、Apple Silicon、带刘海的 MacBook。GPL-3.0 开源，Homebrew 一条命令安装：brew install --cask guokuaile/tally/tally。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Ferry：把一段话交给 AI agent，就能在自家局域网部署一个"给自己发消息"的剪贴板
projects.author: max1874

github.name: max1874/ferry
github.description: Self-hosted clipboard and file ferry for devices on one private network: a single Go server with a built-in web app, so any browser is a client. Native iOS and Android apps are optional.

projects.summary: 协议：Apache-2.0 ｜ 版本：v1.0.0，Docker 镜像支持 amd64 / arm64 一句话 不用读部署文档。把 README 顶部那段话复制给 Claude Code、Codex 这类能在电脑上执行命令的 agent，它会用 Docker 把 Ferry 部署好，然后带你用手机扫码接入，完成第一次文字和文件传输。 部署：交给 agent README 第一节就是一段可以直接复制的提示词（中文版）。里面写清楚了 agent 需要做什么，也写清楚了哪些事不能做： 读 README 和最新 Release，使用发布好的 Compose 部署包和对应镜像，不从源码临时构建； 检查系统、CPU 架构、Docker 和 Compose；缺依赖时先说明并征得你同意，已有部署先备份再升级； 选私有局域网 IP、检查端口，多个网络拿不准时先问你；不暴露到公网，不关防火墙； 部署完检查容器、日志和局域网 HTTP 访问，告诉你访问地址，以及启停、升级、备份的命令； 引导你进入 Devices → Connect another device 扫码，并区分它自己验证过的和仍需要你拿手机确认的，不会把本机检查通过说成跨设备传输成功。 想自己动手的话，README 里也有常规的快速开始，下载 Compose 包，docker compose up -d 即可。 Ferry 是什么 一个自托管的剪贴板与文件摆渡工具，长得像聊天：所有设备共用一条时间线，手机上发的链接、电脑上的截图、一段命令，在另一台设备上点一下就能复制或下载。 设备只需要浏览器。 手机、平板、电脑打开地址就能加入，什么都不用装。 内容不出你的网络。 一个 Go 进程，消息存在 SQLite 里，文件原样保存（单个最大 64 MB，不重新编码）；没有账号、遥测和第三方服务。 是时间线，不是一次性传输。 标注来自哪台设备，明天还能翻到。 剪贴板归你自己。 只在你按粘贴快捷键或点复制按钮时读写，从不在后台读取。 和"给自己发微信"比，内容不经过别人的服务器，截图也不被压缩；和 AirDrop 比，不限苹果设备，而且有可以回翻的历史。 边界 为可信的家庭或办公室私有网络设计，默认是 HTTP，不支持直接暴露到公网；需要 HTTPS 可以自己在内网加一层 Caddy 等反向代理。 iOS 和 Android 原生 App 在仓库里，但不属于 1.0.0 的发布内容，日常使用浏览器即可。 我是作者，自荐。不合适直接关掉即可。

projects.summary: so as a long time Fedora user I just got a macbook for work. while it's so much faster than my old Fedora-based work laptop, it's also running macOS... which I really don't want to learn or get used to. i tried a Fedora VM on the Macbook and even then the modifier keys are still garbled. my friends kept telling i'd simply get used to macOS but i'd like to stick to what i know.. instead of spending some time adjusting to macOS, i spent a few days with an LLM to create a program which uses macOS accessibility features as well as private APIs to make the experience as close to my Fedora computer as possible. it adds some features like a close button in mission control, "snap assist" from windows 10, and the option to remap various keyboard shortcuts to their "normal" equivalents (e.g., ctrl+c -> cmd+c). of course everything can be turned individually on or off. i feel a lot more confident using macOS now after this now that the majority of my muscle memory can transfer over to macos. since the code is written by AI it's licensed under WTFPL. (are AI-generated works even copyrightable?) source code is here: https://github.com/logonoff/superopt

projects.title: Show HN: Threshyr – An offline automatic time tracker with on-device AI
projects.author: affanBajwa
projects.summary: I've built and continuously improved Threshyr based on the problem I faced myself. I was working on more than 3 projects at one time. At the end of any day/week/month if I had to calculate how many hours I have worked on each one, I would always not be able to calculate an accurate time. Because I had to just reconstruct it from memory instead of any real record. Every tracker I tried solved this either by: - sending my activity to their cloud or - by making me press start and stop, which I most of the time forget or - requires a monthly subscription. So I built Threshyr to address all of these pain points. It is a background time tracker for Windows and macOS. It runs entirely locally, recording the duration and window title for active application and active browser(excluding Firefox) domain locally on your machine. It comes up with predefined categories for installed application and browser domain. Each category can be marked as Productive(green color), Neutral(gray color) and Unproductive(red color). Users can modify predefined and can also create their own custom categories. Threshyr utilizes categories, tagging rules and light weight offline AI model called Threshyr AI to classify activity for projects. Users can review the activity classified by Threshyr-AI, can modify the project or even create rules based on the classification. As users review more and more activities, Threshyr-AI gets more accurate with each review. Threshyr lets users see how focused they were, how often and for how long they were distracted, and what was their duration for their productive and unproductive apps and domains. Threshyr also calculates hourly and fixed totals for client projects. Privacy is the core constraint I built this around: - No account, no password, no email required. - No keystroke logging, no screenshots, no behavioral analytics. - Zero cloud inference. - There are exactly two daily network calls: an anonymous daily ping to check for version updates and an active user ping. Threshyr is closed source right now. I am a solo developer in Pakistan trying to build a longer term and sustainable alternative to expensive time trackers. Right now, it is in pre-release. It is completely free to use with no obligation to pay (though there is an optional early-purchase at $29/year if you want to support it). After the pre-release ends Threshyr will be priced at $58 per year. No monthly subscription. I might add a lifetime price. Linux builds and team features are not available yet. Threshyr does not support Firefox I’d appreciate any feedback from the community, especially on how well the classification and tagging rules work for your specific workflows. Also let me know your thoughts about a lifetime price. I'll be in the thread to answer any questions.

projects.author: gentpan

github.name: gentpan/OpenStats
github.description: 轻量原生的 macOS 菜单栏系统监控：CPU、GPU、内存、网络、温度，支持风扇调速与防休眠。Swift 6 + SwiftUI，液态玻璃界面。

projects.summary: 大家好，我是 OpenStats 的开发者，想自荐一个开源的 macOS 菜单栏工具。 想在菜单栏抬眼就看到 CPU、风扇、网速，发现问题后直接调风扇、合盖继续跑、清缓存——所以做了这个中文优先、把「看」和「做」放在一起的工具。 菜单栏九种风格：CPU / GPU / 内存 / 网速 / 磁盘 / 电池 / 温度 / 风扇，双行文字、圆环、饼图、柱状历史等可整体或单项指定；数字等宽，刷新不抖动。 详情弹窗：核心热力图、流量历史与 ping、内存水位、电池与蓝牙外设电量等，区块可关。 温度与风扇：读全部传感器；自动 / 降温 / 强冷 / 自定义四种模式，退出后风扇自动恢复。 防休眠与清理：合盖继续跑任务；按类别清理缓存 / 日志 / 安装包等，清理前二次确认。 进程与本机解释：右键「用 Apple 智能解释」由系统本机模型说明（需 macOS 26，不联网）。 隐私与平台：数据本机读取，无统计上报；仅公网 IP 归属地查询与可选 ping 可联网（可关）。Swift + SwiftUI，无第三方 Swift 包依赖；SMC/风扇相关逻辑参考并移植自 exelban/stats（MIT）。MIT 开源，Developer ID 签名并公证。macOS 14+，Apple Silicon 上开发测试，Intel 风扇与温度未验证。界面有简体中文和英文。

projects.title: Show HN: Pizza Bot – An inbox for AI agents that work in the background
projects.author: jd_

github.name: pizza-bot-app/pizza-bot
github.description: A local-first inbox for long-running AI agents, built with DeepAgents and LangGraph.

projects.summary: Hi HN - long-time lurker (since 2012!), first time poster. Pizza Bot is a self-hosted desktop app for Mac, Windows, and Linux that runs AI agents in the background and exposes them through an email-like UI. Finished work shows up in Unread, and anything waiting on your approval shows up in Action. It's Apache 2.0-licensed, there's no signup and no telemetry, and you bring your own model provider: Anthropic, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, OpenAI, OpenRouter, or a local model through Ollama. There are builds on the releases page, or you can run it from source. Pizza Bot started as an internal passion project I worked on with a small team at Amazon. The whole thing came out of my frustration at having to manually log CRM activities through a browser form. I built a simple REST API called "JoeBot" that connected to my authenticated browser session over CDP and filled out the form for me using Playwright. Then I hacked up a quick Obsidian plugin so I could trigger it from my local notes (no AI and no MCP servers involved). This caught on quickly. My fellow AWS Solutions Architect Igor Fil joined up with me, and we rebranded the project as "Pizza Bot," named after Amazon's two-pizza teams. We started seeing what other automations we could build. We found a GraphQL API we could query and hacked up some "recipes" to pull data out of the CRM to help with meeting prep. That worked great, and it was right around the time MCP servers seemed to be taking off, so we decided to expose Pizza Bot as an MCP server instead, so it would be available to AI tools through natural language. This was a decent solution for technical users, but the Account Managers who live inside our CRM system wanted something too. We decided to rebuild Pizza Bot as an Electron desktop app modeled after an email inbox, so it would be familiar to non-technical users and would run on both Mac and Windows. We also bundled internal MCP servers as OCI images and hosted them in Amazon ECR as an "addon marketplace" so users could install them with one click without having to set up Amazon developer tooling. The project took off organically and expanded outside of AWS into the wider Amazon organization globally. More than 2,000 people ended up using it for meeting prep, email drafting, Slack summaries, CRM logging, prioritizing their day, and web research. Once apps like Claude Cowork and Amazon's own Quick Desktop came out, we realized the real growth opportunity was outside of Amazon. Rather than try to rip out the Amazon-specific integrations, we rebuilt Pizza Bot once more as an open source project. We leaned on coding agents heavily, which is the only reason a team our size could pull off a full rewrite. I'm pleased to say it's finally public, and we're hoping to bring in community members and see where it goes. We'd like to do for knowledge workers what Claude Code and Codex have done for programmers. A couple of things to know up front. Most of what made Pizza Bot useful on day one inside Amazon came from that internal catalog of skills and MCP servers for Amazon's own systems, and none of it could come out with the app. So it ships thinner than the version those 2,000 people used, and building that catalog back up for tools other people actually use is where we need the most help. It's also a community project and not an AWS service, so there's no support or SLA behind it. The Windows and Linux builds aren't signed yet either. On the technical side, Pizza Bot is a server and a client. The desktop app bundles both, or you can point a client at a remote backend; personally, I self-host the server on my home network and reach it from my phone over Tailscale. The server owns the thread lifecycle and checkpoints state with DeepAgents and LangGraph, and clients rehydrate from it as needed, so you can disconnect mid-run and pick the thread back up from another client. Approval pauses outlive the session that created them and collect in an Action filter, so you can answer an hour later from a different device. The agent you talk to has a sandboxed QuickJS interpreter that can reach your filesystem only if you grant it a folder, but its main job is to delegate. Each subagent is a 1:1 mapping of a Skill, and an Activity bar shows that subagent and the tool calls it's making as it works. Memory is opt-in and stored as plain markdown files on your machine. Every tool call is explicit, including looking up a memory - we err on the side of transparency to reduce surprises. Tools come from MCP servers, and skills are ordinary SKILL.md files with a per-tool approval policy, so existing skills that don't require a code interpreter should still work. What I'd most like to hear about is where the app itself gets in your way, the kind of problem you can't fix by writing a skill or an MCP server. I'm around today to answer questions!

projects.author: edwin-hao-ai
projects.summary: 我是 MDDock 的开发者，想自荐一个本地优先的 Markdown 编辑器 + AI 知识库。 起因是我的笔记分散在三处：Obsidian 写日常、Typora 写长文，还有一堆 AI 编程助手（Claude Code / Cursor）当「记忆」写下的 .md 文件，它们互相看不见。MDDock 的思路是直接打开任何一个 .md 文件夹——不导入、不锁定格式，你的文件夹就是知识库本身，可以用 git 管、用任意网盘同步。 几个可能值得一提的点： AI 问答有据可查：索引和搜索全部在本机完成（全文 + 语义），问一个问题，回答会引用具体来自哪个文件。只有当你明确发送问题时，相关内容才经过云端大模型，且首次发送前会征求同意。 给 AI 编程助手当记忆：自带 MCP server 和 CLI，Claude Code / Cursor / Codex 可以直接搜索、读取你的笔记——助手终于记得你上周跟它说过什么。 写作体验完整：Typora 式即时渲染、一键把文档变成幻灯片演示、和 Office 文档双向转换。 免安装的浏览器工具：官网还有一组打开即用的免费 Markdown 在线工具（预览 / 转换 / 表格 / 格式化）。 macOS / Windows / iOS 三端完全免费，闭源。官网 ，iOS 版已上架 App Store。
projects.titleZh: 【工具自荐】MDDock：本地优先的 Markdown 编辑器 + AI 知识库（macOS / Windows / iOS 免费）

projects.titleEn: MDDock: Local-First Markdown Editor and AI Knowledge Base
projects.summaryEn: Local-first Markdown editor and AI knowledge base that opens any .md folder directly with no import or format lock-in.

projects.title: Show HN: Shortcut Express – My attempt to get the world using keyboard shortcuts
projects.author: motomac
projects.summary: I often see people reach for the mouse to select text or close a tab, even when they're already typing. Most know how to copy and paste with the keyboard, but use the mouse for almost everything else. I use the mouse plenty myself, but a few shortcuts have become habits. You don't need to learn that many to find them useful. Things like moving between words or selecting a whole line come up often and are mostly universal across apps and operating systems. I think most people just get used to doing things with the mouse. Learning shortcuts takes a bit of effort, and looking through a cheatsheet doesn't help much if you don't use what you've learned right away. I wanted to make something where you could practice them as you go. That's why I built Shortcut Express, a small desktop app that teaches shortcuts for everyday tasks. You practice them in a simulated text editor, browser and other familiar parts of an app. Completely free and open source. Available for macOS, Windows and Linux. https://github.com/chimit/shortcut-express/releases/latest

projects.title: Show HN: Notula for Google Meet
projects.author: anetrebskii
projects.summary: Hi HN. I built this because quite often all these tools that transcribe save it somewhere in their own storage, so you have to pay for it. And if not the payment, another bigger issue is that this storage is in another place, where I need to copy from. And of course I don't want to pay for storage that I'm not going to use, because I have my own place for such documents and transcriptions. Once I met a nice tool that just records the transcription and does nothing else. You copy the transcription and paste it wherever you want. But at some point it stopped working properly. Then there's another issue. I used it a lot, but it requires you to keep the transcription open all the time, and it takes up space on the Google Meet page. For instance, if someone shares their screen, it's smaller because of the transcription, which I only needed for the extension. So I wanted to make it better, and that's why I built it. On transcription it does the same, it just saves locally, but it doesn't keep the transcription open at all, so you get the full space of your browser in Google Meet. You can copy the transcription to your clipboard and paste it in your place, or download the MD file, whatever you want. And just recently I updated it and made it save to my git repository automatically. You pick the repository, you pick the folder, and it is saved there. That part goes via Notula, my desktop editor, but I don't want to force on you some extra tools that I don't need myself, so everything else works without it. It used to be called MeetScribe, and two identifiers inside it still say meetscribe. They have to. They are how two content scripts find each other, and renaming them breaks every Meet tab that is open at the moment the update lands. I would love it if you would kick the tires and let me know what you think of it. Happy meetings! --- Website: https://notula.org/meet/ Chrome Web Store: https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/notula-for-google-m... GitHub: https://github.com/anetrebskii/meetscribe

projects.title: 【软件自荐】AtAt：在 Mac 任意输入框调用 Claude Code、Codex，少一点复制粘贴
projects.author: xinyao27
projects.summary: 我是 AtAt 的开发者，想自荐一个原生 Mac 工具。 平时用 Claude Code、Codex，总要把屏幕上的内容、选中的文字和文件搬进终端，再把结果复制回来。AtAt 想省掉这段来回：在输入框打 @@，把截图、文字、剪贴板内容或 Finder 文件带给自己的 agent；回答先预览，确认后按 Tab 插回原处。需要继续做复杂任务时，也能把上下文交给终端里的交互式 agent。 此外，它也能独立用于截图、录屏、剪贴板历史和划词操作。模型或 agent 使用用户自己的账号与配置，提示词不经过 AtAt 的服务器。 官网及演示： 系统：macOS 15+，仅支持 Apple silicon。 试用：7 天完整功能，无需 AtAt 账号或银行卡。 价格：$9/月、$59/年或 $169 买断；早鸟为 $49/年、$119 买断，截止 2026-10-08（UTC）。价格未含适用税费。 欢迎试用，也希望听听大家在把现有 agent 接进日常 Mac 工作流时遇到的问题。 功能演示视频 在输入框输入 @@，直接调用自己的 agent 选中文字，让 agent 调整语气 框选屏幕内容，带着截图提问 查看和使用剪贴板历史 在 Finder 中调用 AtAt 拖入文件作为上下文 把复杂任务交给终端中的交互式 agent 完整

projects.title: Show HN: Quickly generate and explain complex shell commands
projects.author: buster
projects.summary: Hi everyone, as I spent a substantial amount of time in the console, even today, i sometimes need to think of some complex combination of git/find/ffmpeg/xargs and friends and so i've been using https://github.com/kagisearch/ask for some time. Since it appears to be unmaintained i started my own version (yes, thanks to some LLMs work) and i am quite happy with it. It appears to have gained a lot more features than i initially thought but there it is. My personal highlights are: - can install shortcuts for bash/fish/zsh for pressing CTRL-W and having the current prompt replaced with the "answer" $ find all images in this directory becomes $ find . -type f \( -iname '*.jpg' -o -iname '*.jpeg' -o -iname '*.png' -o -iname '*.gif' -o -iname '*.bmp' -o -iname '*.webp' -o -iname '*.svg' -o -iname '*.tiff' \) in 1-2 seconds. - there is also a review TUI that explains the commands (which can become complex) or retries with another model In any case, it's open source, maybe someone else will find it useful as well.

projects.summary: Hey HN, I’ve been cobbling together a tool to read beautifully formatted markdown without leaving my terminal. Lime renders markdown in the terminal with actual formatting - big headers, syntax highlighted code, mermaid diagrams, all drawn using Ghostty’s Kitty graphics protocol support. It picks up your terminal’s native theme and you can jump between headings, pull up a table of contents to search and jump to sections of your document. It’s macOS and Ghostty for now, the document lives in scroll back and we use Apple Events to ask Ghostty jump around the scroll back instead of re-rendering. This also lets you use Ghostty’s native search and shortcuts for navigation.

projects.title: Show HN: SideNote Pro – Native Windows 11 AI beside your work
projects.author: fortisnode
projects.summary: I have been using ChatGPT (mainly) as my main AI tool, but sometimes also DeepSeek and other AI providers. But with repetitive tasks, it became annoying for me to switch tabs and navigate to the ChatGPT tab in the web browser, leaving the Excel document and my focus behind just for a quick question, some text processing, or image identification. This is how I came up with the idea of having an assistant right beside the workspace that can be pinned and docked to the side of the display. On today's wide displays, it fits really well. It has a visible handle/leash on the right side of the display and can be invoked via a keyboard shortcut. I find myself using it often because a question in Photoshop or Premiere Pro doesn't require me to leave to open the browser; I can just invoke it and get the response quickly. So, it started to become more than a simple chatbox, adding features such as file indexing in a selected folder. It also supports uploading images or screenshots, or directly pasting image crops into the composer. Also, a nice feature I like a lot is that you can assign a prompt/action to a global shortcut and run it on the selected text. For instance, it can translate a paragraph by selecting the paragraph and pressing the keyboard shortcut Ctrl+Shift+T; the assistant will appear and stream the answer. It supports BYOK (bring your own key) and OpenAI-compatible AI providers, as well as local ones such as Ollama, making it an easy frontend for a locally running LLM. It is built natively for Windows 11 in C# and is available for download from the Microsoft Store. I am very interested to hear whether you find switching tabs annoying and whether such a tool could help.

It recognizes 20+ details (prices, orders, codes, links) and infers why you saved it: buy later, track, read later. Fully private: no cloud, no account. Nothing ever leaves your phone. projects.title: Show HN: Runyte – a modal editor with integrated terminals and a file manager
projects.author: boredCoconut
projects.summary: Hi, I'm building Runyte, an open-source terminal workspace built around a modal text editor, written in Rust. The goal is to create a coherent workspace with minimal UI and maximum focus. Files, terminal panes, and Git views share one interface, navigation, clipboard, and theme. A fuzzy finder searches through files, buffers, and terminals. Runyte supports a persistent mode (client-server) in which you can detach and return later while terminal processes and LSP servers keep running, or you can switch directly to another Git worktree. There are also some features to minimize the friction when working with CLI coding agents: markdown rendering, image pasting, editing agent prompts, searching terminal sessions with the fuzzy finder or regex. It's pre-1.0, but fully usable. Works on Linux and MacOS. You can download a binary or install it with cargo install runyte --locked. There's an interactive tutorial :tutorial. I'd especially appreciate feedback on navigating between editing, terminals, and worktrees, and where the interface interrupts your concentration.

projects.title: Show HN: Live audio dubbing from any browser tab
projects.author: christiansafka
projects.summary: Hey HN, at Pinch we've been working on something to reduce friction to getting accurate, fast audio translation for live media. Initially we launched a desktop app that sat between your hardware mic/speakers and your meeting platform, but this required users to install our audio driver which introduced permissions hoops to jump through as well as stability issues across updates, not to mention trying to get our device driver approved by Microsoft.. So today we're launching Pinch Sidecar, which offers speech to speech translation in-browser for any Chrome browser tab. This is accomplished by sharing the tab audio with our page, where we proceed to mute the original tab and mix in our translated audio with speaker-matched voices. We also offer meeting creators using Google Meet, Zoom, or Teams the ability to host a translated meeting where listeners can listen and interact in their own language through our Sidecar. The tab translation mode is open for free testing for this HN launch. Our ask is just to let us know how it goes, and to share the link to anyone you know organizing multilingual webinars/meetings.

projects.summary: 大家好，分享一下我做的小工具 Kiri ，免费开源，支持 macOS 和 Windows 。 平时截个图、标一下重点，或者从图片里复制一段文字，就可以用它。按快捷键后选窗口或框一块区域，截图可以加箭头、文字和马赛克，也可以直接识别文字，或者录成 MP4 / GIF 。 截图和录屏会放进本地图库，可以按名字、标签查找。OCR 默认在本机运行；如果自己配置了远程 OCR ，每次上传前也需要确认。 官网放了操作演示，可以先看看用起来是什么样： - 官网与演示： https://kiri.yuxino.cn/zh/#demo - 源码： https://github.com/yuxino/kiri - 下载： https://github.com/yuxino/kiri/releases/latest 目前需要 macOS 14+ 或 Windows 11 x64 。macOS 安装包还没有 Apple 公证，首次打开可能要到「隐私与安全性」里点「仍要打开」； Windows 安装包也没有 Authenticode 签名，可能会遇到 SmartScreen 提示。 这个小工具花了不少时间打磨，希望大家用着顺手 (˶ᵔ ᵕ ᵔ˶) 有不顺手的地方，欢迎告诉我，最好带上系统版本和复现步骤，我会继续改。

projects.title: DrawDog
projects.summary: Clients are starting to ask freelancers to prove their work wasn't generated. DrawDog sits in your menu bar and records how your file grew, what apps were in front of you, and whether an AI tool was ever open. It signs and timestamps that record, then gives you one link to send. The client drags your file onto the page to confirm it's the one you certified. It never looks inside your work: no screen recording, no keystrokes, no file names. Three certificates a month, free.

projects.title: Show HN: Rdltr – Inbox zero for your reading list
projects.author: eduardosasso
projects.summary: Hi HN, for the past few months I’ve been working on a read later app called RDLTR ( https://rdltr.app ). The whole thing started because I had so many tabs open with stuff I wanted to read, across browsers, Mac, Linux, and iPhone. They cluttered everything and got in the way of other things I had to do. Pocket had just shut down when this idea came up, I looked around, tried Instapaper, Raindrop, Matter, and a few others I forget. They were fine, but they all give you a list that only grows, which is another thing to maintain, and not the model I had in mind. Safari has this Reading List feature where you read something and it drops off the unread list. But it’s Apple only and half worked. What I wanted was inbox zero for reading. Open something, read it, come back, and it’s gone from the queue but still in the archive. You keep going until there is nothing left. Links come in from anywhere. Paste a URL on the page, drag one in, or use the bookmarklet, the Chrome and Firefox extensions, or the Apple Shortcut for the iOS share sheet, plus Vim keys, TL;DR summaries on each link, search across everything you have read or saved, RSS for every list, and it works just as well on the phone. The extensions have a couple of tricks that I use all the time. Shift+DD pulls the article text, cleans it up, and sends it to ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini in a new tab, so you can ask it anything about what you just read. Shift+AA opens it in the Internet Archive, handy for paywalled sites when you don’t have a subscription. The stack is Bun, TypeScript, HTMX, and SQLite, with SSE so the list updates the moment you save or read something, deployed on a Hetzner VPS. Full disclosure, Claude Code wrote most of it. I still spent a ton of time dogfooding, testing, and polishing the UI until things felt right. Anyway, curious to know what your current setup is for this.

projects.title: Revindo
projects.summary: Two pieces: a desktop app holding the AI agent, and a Chrome extension that acts inside your own Vinted session. You type a plain instruction and the agent drafts the listing, suggests a price anchored on real completed sales rather than the last displayed price, prepares buyer replies, and surfaces underpriced items to resell. No cloud bot touches your account, and a STOP button stays visible. Vinted in production; Leboncoin under construction.

projects.title: Stash
projects.summary: Stash is a Mac screenshot, screen recording, and clipboard app built for working with AI. Captures carry app, window, and accessibility context. Recordings can become AI reports with transcripts, interactions, and keyframes. Annotate screenshots, keep clipboard history, and share video demos by link. Free during public beta. macOS 14+.

projects.title: 330+ 开源的多款免费在线计算器与单位转换器，MIT 协议
projects.author: ctolib-oss

github.name: PDFCraftTool/OmniTools
github.description: 330+ free calculators and converters. Fast, accurate, and easy to use.

projects.summary: 一套使用 Next.js 14 开发，包含 300 多个免费在线计算器与转换器的综合工具集。包括金融、健康、家居与手工、单位转换器、效率工具。

projects.title: Vibe Eyes
projects.summary: I miss my dog when I am at my desk all day. So now he lives in my menu bar. Drop in a photo and Vibe Eyes turns your own pet into a tiny animated avatar up there. It follows your cursor, blinks at you, winks when you click and looks up when you have been away. Small stuff, but you catch yourself glancing up and smiling. Eleven pets built in, free. Making your own is a $14.99 one-time unlock plus your own AI key. No subscription, no backend, your photo never touches my server.

projects.title: mactap
projects.summary: MacTap is a free, open-source macOS menu bar app that turns knocks on your MacBook chassis into shortcuts. One, two, or three knocks copy, paste, accept an AI suggestion, take a screenshot, control media, or anything you map. It reads the accelerometer inside the unibody (the same sensor that detects if your laptop is falling) and classifies knocks on-device. Nothing gets uploaded, no account, no network calls. Just a small native Swift app sitting in your menu bar.

projects.title: Flash Mask
projects.author: sudohg
projects.summary: Flash Mask 是一款帮助你在与 AI 或 Agent 协作时，清楚说明图片中哪个位置需要修改的辅助工具。当你需要让 AI 修改图片中的某个局部区域时，只需拖入图片，圈出一处或多处区域，即可快速生成记录圈选位置和修改要求的 JSON 数据，省去在大型图像软件中反复框选、导出的繁琐步骤。 典型使用场景包括：当你只想让 AI 修改图片中的某个细节时，圈出需要处理的区域，例如角色图中的手、脸或配件，照片背景里的路人或杂物，海报中的局部元素；也可以为 Coding Agent 标记 UI 截图中的问题位置，如 iOS Simulator、原生 App、Canvas、WebGL、地图、图表或游戏 UI 中的文字截断、控件重叠和布局错位。一次可标记多个区域，并将位置与修改要求一起交给 Agent。 主要功能： • 快速标记区域：拖入图片后直接圈选一处或多处需要修改的区域，并可附加文字说明。 • 一键复制 JSON：默认将包含图片路径和尺寸、区域坐标及可选修改要求的 JSON 数据复制到剪贴板，可直接粘贴给正在使用的 Agent，无需先导出蒙版。 • 导出黑白蒙版：需要更精细的处理时，可导出与原图尺寸一致的黑白蒙版。白色表示圈选区域，黑色表示其他区域。 • 支持的图片格式：PNG、JPEG/JPG、WebP。 Flash Mask 负责生成位置数据和蒙版，实际的图片修改由你使用的 AI 或 Agent 完成。 所有图片和蒙版均在本机处理，可离线使用，无需账户。

projects.title: Gojo
projects.summary: Gojo puts local dictation, clipboard history, window controls, a file shelf, and media controls in your MacBook notch. Download a speech model, then dictate into the field you're using. Recognition runs on your Mac in local mode. Includes calendar, battery, camera, and display controls. macOS 14+. Three-day trial; monthly and one-time licenses.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】mimi：给正在播放的视频加上实时翻译字幕
projects.author: yuxino

github.name: yuxino/mimi
github.description: Live translated subtitles for anything playing on your Mac or PC.

projects.summary: 大家好，自荐一个我做的开源实时字幕工具 mimi。 看外语视频、课程或直播时，内容不一定自带字幕。mimi 直接识别电脑正在播放的声音，将字幕和翻译显示在画面上，不依赖视频网站提供字幕。 主要功能 实时字幕与翻译：从系统音频生成字幕，按服务商能力翻译成简体中文、英语或日语。 沉浸模式：用快捷键隐藏面板和按钮，只让字幕文字留在画面上。 字幕浮窗：支持移动、缩放、暂停和点击穿透，可以按自己的观看习惯调整。 开始使用 目前支持 Apple 芯片 Mac（macOS 13+），也提供 Windows x64 预览版。下载后配置翻译服务，播放内容，再从菜单栏或系统托盘点击「开始」。 需要自备服务商 API 凭证，调用可能产生费用。 系统音频发送给所选服务商处理，mimi 本身不保存音频或字幕。 演示视频 视频展示英文片段的翻译字幕和沉浸模式切换，采用真实服务结果回放，并非安装版端到端实录。录制说明与素材来源 项目采用 MIT 协议开源，欢迎试用和反馈。 项目源码 · 下载安装 ·

projects.title: CutX
projects.summary: macOS has no cut for files: Finder's ⌘X is greyed out, and the real move gesture (⌘C then ⌥⌘V) is one almost nobody knows. CutX makes the obvious shortcut do the obvious thing. Press ⌘X on a file or folder, then ⌘V where you want it. The items move. CutX never touches your files — it asks Finder to do the move, so undo, progress, Replace/Keep Both and permission prompts all work as usual. Outside Finder, ⌘X still cuts text. Free, open source, no tracking. 11 languages, incl. mirrored Arabic.

projects.title: Cloveworks
projects.summary: Hold Option while dragging any file in Finder and a radial menu appears under your cursor. Drop it on Rename, Summarize, Extract Text, Transcribe, or Explain and the result lands next to the original, with Undo in the menu bar. Everything runs on-device with Apple's models in macOS 26: no account, no upload, no telemetry. Needs no Accessibility permission. 25 free actions, then a one-time purchase.

projects.title: FlokinMD
projects.summary: FlokinMD is an open-source, local-first desktop app that treats your Markdown files as structured data. Explore collections, frontmatter, relations, graphs, SQL, workspace health, bulk edits, and AI context — while keeping yourmd files as the source of truth.

projects.title: ClickScrape
projects.summary: ClickScrape is a Chrome extension for pulling structured data off a webpage without writing code or paying a monthly scraping subscription. Click the fields you want on the page. ClickScrape collects them from every matching item, follows pagination and infinite scroll as you browse, and can follow each item's link for detail-page fields. Export to Excel, CSV or JSON, copy to clipboard, or download images as a ZIP. $5.99 one-time, no subscription. Runs locally in your browser.

projects.title: Ergoblin
projects.summary: You call this a hunt? Your ancestors ran antelope to death over 2 days to survive. You've been slouching in that chair scrolling product launches while your eyes dry up into raisins. I see where we are. I'm a mouthy goblin who lives in your menu bar who asks for basic human functions your body is begging for. There are 7 kinds of neglect on my list and you're doing at least 4 right now. I have moods. Put me off and I get less polite. Tell me you can't and I make the ask smaller. Mac and Windows.

projects.title: Verdant
projects.summary: A desktop app designed for the lifecycle of your ideas: capture thoughts, track your cognitive energy, and synthesize projects. Verdant features an ink-and-paper aesthetic and a local-first architecture — your data never leaves your machine. Use our BYOK (Bring Your Own Key) model to connect OpenAI or Anthropic at raw API cost, or hook up a local model for 100% private, air-gapped synthesis. Available for Mac, Windows, and Linux.

projects.title: DockSwitcher
projects.summary: DockSwitcher is a lightweight macOS menu bar utility that lets you create multiple Dock profiles and switch between them instantly.

projects.title: ScreamCursor
projects.summary: ScreamCursor is a cursed Windows desktop app that screams when you shake your mouse. Build power, trigger ridiculous reactions, and unlock transformations. The core experience is free, with the $9.99 Ascended Warrior Bundle for extra chaos.

projects.title: NeoTalker
projects.summary: While modern TTS apps push heavy cloud AI and costly subscriptions, NeoTalker takes a radically fast, privacy-first route. Built with Rust and Tauri, it revives the classic, crystal-clear PicoTTS engine in an ultra-lightweight desktop app (~25MB, <50MB RAM). Features: • Featherweight footprint • Offline privacy: zero telemetry • Unrestricted exports: queue hours of audios to MP3/OGG/WAV • DSP vibrato & smart text normalizer • Nostalgic pricing: pay once, keep forever. Built for Windows by Yeib.

projects.title: PIXU
projects.summary: PIXU is a fast and free, cross-platform terminal image viewer for developers. View images in RGB, grayscale, 256-color, ASCII, Kitty/iTerm2 or Sixel, with interactive browsing, clipboard input, pipelines, resizing, rotation and dithering.

projects.title: PelOptimo 2026.1
projects.summary: Filter and transform thousands of images with enterprise CLI using Local AI. Filter images with 80 built-in classes of smart objects. PelOptimo Pro combines intelligent image optimization, object-aware processing, and high-speed batch automation into a single desktop application. Designed for professionals who need maximum performance without sacrificing privacy.

projects.title: Bezel
projects.summary: Menubar capture. Pick Window or Region, hit Copy. Gets a 16:9 framed PNG with titlebar + soft shadow on your clipboard. Save if you want a file. Screen Recording permission on first use. Personal license, up to 2 Macs.

projects.title: Show HN: MacTap, use knocks on your MacBook as shortcuts
projects.author: jaskirat16
projects.summary: I was playing with the motion sensor inside my MacBook and noticed that knocks on the aluminum next to the trackpad showed up very clearly. That turned into MacTap. You can map different knock patterns to actions like copy, paste, screenshots, AI actions, music controls, and more. It runs locally and it’s open source.

projects.title: Ampel
projects.summary: See when Claude Code needs you without switching terminals. Ampel puts a traffic light in your Mac menu bar: red when blocked on your input, yellow while working, green when idle. Track multiple sessions by project and optionally see your 5-hour and 7-day plan usage. Free, open source, and native to macOS 14+.

projects.title: ClipForge
projects.summary: ClipForge is a free Windows tool that watches your clipboard for video URLs. Copy a link from YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, or other platforms — it automatically downloads the video and copies the MP4 file back to your clipboard. Press Ctrl+V anywhere to paste the actual video. No ads, no sign-ups, no tracking. Just one step: copy link → paste video. Supported: YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, X, Reddit, Vimeo, Dailymotion, Twitch, Streamable, Rumble

projects.title: Show HN: Browser only CSV editor, data never leaves your machine
projects.author: anshulsahni
projects.summary: The current software I am working upon as part of my full time job, I have to deal with very long JSONs and lot of CSVs. For editing or viewing JSONs my first and obivous choice was jsonher.io, it’s the most wonderful JSON viewer I have ever seen. But I wish I could the same for CSVs too, when I googled it, I couldn’t find anything good. Most of the tools were asking me to sign up, some of them allowed me to open CSV but then came a big popup asking for my credit card so that I can edit it or use some filters, and lot of them were sending CSV to server in case it was large. I will be honest, there were some which were no signup or no server, but their UX was bad - sublime was showing the content better than those. Then I started building one for myself, and it turns out building no signup, browser only CSV tool is actually possible even for managing large CSVs; I was able to make it up and running within days and it turns out to be awesome - apologies for shameless bragging. Later I added support for downloading content in JSON and other alternatives of CSV like PSV, TSV, SSV, etc. It has all the basic functionalities for working with CSVs - filtering, sorting, editing, deleting, downloading in your desired format. In near future, I am planning to make it one shot CSV editor for all kinds of platform - browser extensions, desktop app and hopefully mobile apps too ( I am bad at building mobile apps, but I will try my best ). Do check it out and let me know in comments, what you feel about it.

projects.title: StatusPerch
projects.summary: StatusPerch is a small native macOS utility for hiding the menu bar icons you rarely need. Hold Command to move compatible icons to the left of its boundary, then use the chevron to hide or reveal that group. It runs locally, needs no account, and its core workflow requires neither Screen Recording nor Accessibility access. Version 1.0 is free for Apple silicon and Intel Macs, with English and Simplified Chinese.

projects.title: Trancy Air
projects.summary: Trancy Air is a shortcut-driven translator that sits ready on macOS and Windows. In any app: select what you can't read and it's translated; write in your own language and one key swaps it to another; too lazy to type, just talk. It also catches mistakes, polishes wording, reads text aloud and scores your pronunciation.

projects.title: Matrix Desktop
projects.summary: Matrix Desktop renders live Matrix digital rain behind your windows and as a screensaver. Built natively for Apple Silicon Macs with Metal, it offers adjustable presets and menu bar controls. Multiple displays are supported, with power and thermal backoff for laptops. Free, with no account or subscription. Requires macOS 14+.

projects.title: Nexora Tools
projects.summary: Nexora Tools brings nine everyday utilities into one clean Windows desktop app. Generate QR codes, format JSON, resize images, create passwords, generate UUIDs, encode Base64, convert timestamps, calculate hashes, and pick colors—all locally on your device. No uploads, no accounts, no ads, and no subscription.

projects.title: Loadstone
projects.summary: Loadstone is a tiny Swift menubar app that snaps the frontmost Mac window to halves, corners, thirds, and two-thirds — keyboard or drag-to-edge. Free open-source Magnet-style option: no Electron, no dock icon, signed and notarized, Apple Silicon, macOS 14+. Install: brew install --cask mortenbrudvik/tap/loadstone

projects.title: Scatti
projects.summary: Scatti is a desktop app for culling RAW shoots locally: justified grid, pick/reject/stars with auto-advance, 100% zoom for focus checks, then copy or move picks and trash rejects (with sidecars). It shows each camera’s embedded JPEG preview—no demosaic, import waiting room, or cloud. Built for working photographers on Linux (also Windows x86_64 and macOS Apple Silicon). €19 founder license (2 devices), 14-day trial, no account. Not a RAW developer or AI picker. Builds are unsigned for now.

projects.title: Veilary
projects.summary: Veilary turns private photo storage into a real workflow. Keep photos and videos in separate iPhone spaces with album passcodes, Face ID or Touch ID, decoy content, and face-down quick hide. Then open Veilary on the same trusted Wi-Fi network from a desktop browser to create albums, organize media, and upload or download files—no desktop client or Veilary cloud photo library required. Nearby iPhone-to-iPhone transfer and password-protected backup archives keep migration practical.

projects.title: Show HN: Gote – a CLI note-taking management tool for plain Markdown
projects.author: banorton
projects.summary: Repo: https://github.com/banorton/gote I built a note taking management tool to use at work for quick note taking and searching. It is intended to be quite minimal. Another focus was to have lots of shortcuts and to keep things close to the homerow for ergonomics and speed. Notes are just markdown files in whatever directory you point it at. The only thing it keeps elsewhere is an index in ~/.gote. If you stop using it you still have all your notes. Tags go on the first line of the note, separated by periods, like .project.urgent.work. No frontmatter. Search is built into the binary, BM25 with stemming, so there's no ripgrep or fzf to set up. gote s meeting searches titles and content, gote s -t .work filters by tag, gote s -w 2412 pulls up notes from December 2024. Most commands have a two letter version that combines a list with an action. ro is recent + open, sv is search + view, tp is tag + pin. When results come up you pick one with a home row key instead of arrows or numbers. Binaries for mac/linux/windows are on the releases page, or go install github.com/banorton/gote@latest if you have Go. The goal of this project was not to learn something new or build something impressive. I simply had a need and filled it with a vibe-coded solution. I have been using it for about a year now and it does more or less exactly what I wanted. So I thought I'd share in case others are interested in using it, contributing to it, or want to use it as a reference for their own solution.

projects.title: AI Chat Exporter
projects.summary: AI Chat Exporter is a free, open-source browser extension for taking your AI conversations with you. Export chats from ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Copilot, Perplexity, DeepSeek, Qwen, Meta AI and more to Markdown, JSON, HTML, PDF, Word or PNG. Everything is processed locally in your browser. No accounts, no cloud processing, and no chat data sent to third-party servers. It also supports clipboard rich-text copying, chat continuation between AI platforms, custom filenames and a browser side panel.

projects.title: kiddyproof
projects.summary: one shortcut and your Mac's keyboard and trackpad stop reaching any app, but the screen stays looking exactly how you left it (Slack open, half-typed message and all). your kid can go ham on the keys and none of it lands, they just get calm glowing light to poke at. exit is a deliberate 3-second parent hold. signed and notarized, no account, no cloud.

projects.title: Lyrimuse
projects.summary: Word-synced desktop lyrics for Apple Music, Spotify, QQ Music, NetEase, Kugou, and for YouTube Music or Spotify Web in a browser. Nine lyric providers are queried at once and every candidate is scored on one scale — title, artist, album, duration fit, word-level timing — so live takes, Cantonese versions and radio edits get the words that actually match. Shows up as a floating overlay, a Dynamic Island capsule, an Apple-Music-style window, or in the menu bar. Free and open source, no account.

projects.title: Notchful
projects.summary: You already spend your day at the desk. That's where the water should get logged. Notchful lives in your MacBook notch. Hover to see today's progress. Click once to log a drink. Keep working. Nothing to open. Nothing to unlock. By the time you close your laptop, you've already hit your hydration goal without thinking about it. History by week, month, and year. Goal and cup size in Settings. Everything else from the menu bar.

projects.title: AppGacha
projects.summary: AppGacha turns a plain-language wish into a real desktop app—utilities, widgets, games, and personal tools. Apps run locally, stay portable, and can be organized into your own desktop workspace.

projects.title: MenuBar Notes
projects.summary: Capture a thought without leaving what you’re doing. MenuBar Notes is a compact, Mac-native notes app built for quick capture, focused writing and privacy.

projects.title: WordSmart – Automatic Word Formatting
projects.summary: WordSmart is an early Windows desktop tool that automates repetitive Microsoft Word formatting. It helps format headings, paragraphs, tables, fonts, spacing, and alignment while keeping documents consistent. It also supports large documents and ready-made formatting templates. We’re launching this early MVP to learn from real users, understand their Word workflows, and decide which formatting problems and features to focus on next.

projects.title: Slit — make your Mac unstoppable
projects.summary: Slit is a macOS menu bar app that watches memory pressure, quits idle apps, cleans junk, and finds duplicate files. Free to monitor. One purchase to clean.

projects.title: Liang
projects.summary: Liang is a small macOS menu bar app that shows your AI coding agent's state on your screen, no more switching back to check. A soft glow around the notch, a glow following your cursor, and a menu bar icon show whether your agent (Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, CodeBuddy) is thinking, waiting, or done. Each state has its own color. It uses each IDE's official hooks and is local-first: no account, no telemetry, no cloud, and never reads your code or prompts. macOS 14+ and Apple Silicon only.

projects.title: Pastea
projects.summary: Pastea is a clipboard history manager for macOS. It saves every link, snippet and screenshot you copy, so you can search, pin and paste it back in seconds.

projects.title: Show HN: Flying Letters and a Clean Keyboard That Even Steve Jobs Would Like
projects.author: vitalipom
projects.summary: Everyone talks about the negative impact of the screens, but have you been wondering recently around, imagining you’re typing something with some imaginary keyboard? Keyboards differ, some have more memojies, some ultra-high-4k-super-dooper keyboards like Samsung’s app store’s Cafe Keyboard have even plenty of effects. But there is one keyboard, very well hidden, called Effectedkeyboard2 which is not just neatly designed, but also has a feature non of the other keyboards has - flying letters, like in Harry Potter movies, that in addition to all other effects this keyboard offers, this particular effect flies letters as you type - with animation, into your screen! If you happened to stop to try it out, check out some another amazing features that it has: such as more convenient typing caret mover. Long press spacebar till it turns blue and voila, you can drag your fingers through the regular keys to move typing caret even after the phone restarts! Very handy in long text editing. Or else undo/redo options. Have you deleted something useful? Just like in Anysoftkeyboard, which this keyboard is originally based on, swipe up from the spacebar and there you have undo/redo options and on a long press on the paste icon even a clipboard. Unlike Anysoftkeyboard however, Effectedkeyboard2 refreshes its emojies with modern shiny emojies. It has additional visual effects as you type - which mostly cost a couple of dollars, but each is available for a preview under Effects menu in the main settings. Effectedkeyboard2 has been crafted by its developer Vitali Pom. Over the course of 15 years and is now waiting for you to try it out. https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.vitali.pom... Got any questions? Let me know what you think here in the comments.

projects.title: Viewlyt Studio
projects.summary: Jahaan har pal ek yaad ban jaaye. - ViewLyt The simple way for photographers to deliver event photos. Send a private gallery your clients pick from on their phone, or put a QR at the event so guests scan a selfie and get every photo of themselves. Free desktop app — your clients get a free app too.

projects.title: Flick for Mac
projects.summary: Flick is a radial command wheel for macOS. Hold a key, flick your mouse toward an action, release. Launch apps, snap windows, take screenshots, run scripts and Shortcuts, paste clipboard text, control media: one gesture for all of it. Free tier: one wheel of 8 slots, 7 action categories, no account, no time limit. Pro is $19.99 once for up to 5 Macs, with a 30-day free trial.

projects.title: StandBye
projects.summary: StandBye is a bring-your-own-keys Desktop app. Describe a team of AI agents and they keep working on your repo around the clock: they check in, talk in channels, ask you only when a decision is yours, and remember what they learn.

projects.title: LUFScale
projects.summary: Hi Product Hunt! I’m Philippe, the creator and maintainer of LUFScale. LUFScale is a free, open-source desktop app for macOS and Windows that analyzes perceived loudness and normalizes audio to a chosen LUFS target with True Peak control. It supports MP3, FLAC, WAV, AIFF, M4A, OGG and Opus, offers before-and-after comparison, ReplayGain metadata and CSV reports, and never modifies or moves the original files.

projects.title: Show HN: Hush – Brown noise and a speech blocker in the macOS menu bar
projects.author: oldmanrahul
projects.summary: A MacOS menu bar app for brown/speech blocker noise. I've been using online "white noise" generators for over a decade because I find they reliably help me get in the zone for an hour or two of work. I didn't like the context switching cost of needing to find the active browser tab, so I created a mac menu bar app that makes it almost frictionless to enable/disable brown noise. How to try it: See releases zip on the GH repo. It's macOS 13+, notarized. Technical details: - brown noise via leaky integration - a low-pass, speech blocker via pink noise through a 10-band EQ - all synthesized in real time via AVAudioEngine There's also a pay-what-you-want page on Gumroad: https://rahulp6.gumroad.com/l/hush Always open to feedback or comments if this helps you in any way. TY!

projects.title: CopyClipOSS
projects.summary: Menu bar clipboard history for macOS. Encrypted at rest and locked behind Touch ID.

projects.title: Kodo
projects.summary: Kodo is a lightweight, modular IDE for Windows, with Linux support in the works. Itskox extension system lets you add syntax highlighting, themes, plugins, and smart editing features without bloating the core. Kodo includes Build & Run, an integrated terminal, Project Search, customizable shortcuts, and Insight code completion. Open source under GPL-v3.0, Kodo is developed by SS-YYC and KerbalMissile.

projects.title: 猫在｜把真实的它，带回桌面

projects.title: TetherShot

No account. No upload. No AirPlay hacks. Why bookmark it: • iPhone USB + Wi‑Fi + Android ADB in one app • Pixel-perfect — actual device frame, not a mirror • Menu bar + global hotkey from any app • 100% local. Zero telemetry. MIT open source • Homebrew, signed DMG, or npm For devs and creators who screenshot phones daily.

projects.title: OmniDock
projects.summary: One Mac app for the little shortcuts you use all day. Preview windows from the Dock, click a Dock icon again to hide its app, snap windows into place, and find what you copied earlier. App hotkeys, Finder actions, and menu bar controls are built in too. Moving from Windows? Keep familiar window habits without juggling separate utilities. Free and open source. No account needed; optional clipboard history stays on your Mac. macOS 12.3+, Apple silicon and Intel.

projects.title: Bloop
projects.summary: Bloop turns system audio or mic input into eight real-time shader skins - every frame reacts to what's actually playing. Keep it beside your work in the resizable Mini Player or send it to the menu bar. Drop in an MP3 playlist and export the whole thing as a finished video. Apple Silicon, notarized, no subscription. Two skins are free forever, and they're the full app, not a trial.

projects.title: Codex Usage
projects.summary: See every Codex usage limit, reset time, pace, and banked reset from your Mac menu bar. Pressure Check shows which limit you’re using faster than an even pace. Includes a local dashboard and CLI, with no signup or third-party backend.

projects.title: Sidq
projects.summary: You spend an hour getting Claude to understand your project. Then you open ChatGPT and start over from zero. Again. Sidq reads the conversations your AI assistants already write to your own Mac and carries the whole thing into whichever one you open next. One shortcut. Nothing is uploaded, nothing leaves your machine it works with the wifi off. Reads Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Gemini, Copilot, Cursor and more. Native Mac app, written in Rust, notarized by Apple. Free to start.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】DeepDeck：支持 WebMCP 和网页工具生成的 Harness 桌面客户端
projects.author: jo32

github.name: jo32/DeepDeck
github.description: DeepDeck — an extensible desktop workspace for DeepSeek Harness.

projects.summary: 我做了 DeepDeck，一个基于 DeepSeek Harness 的开源桌面客户端，当前提供 Apple Silicon 和 Intel Mac 安装包，采用 MIT 协议。 它内置了一个支持 WebMCP 的浏览器：Agent 可以发现并调用网站提供的工具。对于尚未提供工具的网站，用户描述任务，Builder 会尝试网页操作、检查结果，并将可行的操作保存成可复用工具。 例如，在 X 上构建搜索、读取帖子、编辑和检查草稿的工具后，后续任务可以直接调用。工具源码和版本保存在本地，支持查看、禁用和回退；网站发生变化时，需要重新验证或修改工具。生成工具与网站原生工具分别标明来源。 首次构建工具需要额外探索和验证，节省的时间与 token 取决于后续任务，尚未发布量化对比。 项目源码 中文介绍与演示截图 下载最新版 Harness 社区中的完整介绍（中文在前，英文在后） 这是社区维护的非官方客户端。模型与凭据沿用 Harness 的配置。

projects.title: AI Coach
projects.summary: Hatch an egg, raise a desktop pet, and watch its looks and personality develop. AI Coach connects with Claude and shows its activity through your pet. Everyday tools unlock as it grows. For Mac, with your first egg included free.

projects.title: [开源推荐] Lyrimuse：一个智能匹配歌词的 macOS 桌面歌词工具（自荐）
projects.author: Yudaotor

github.name: Yudaotor/lyrimuse
github.description: Word-synced desktop lyrics on macOS for Apple Music, Spotify, QQ Music, NetEase Cloud Music, Kugou — and YouTube Music / Spotify Web in any browser. Actively maintained open-source LyricsX alternative. Floating overlay, Dynamic Island, menu bar or lyrics window; translation, romanization, Last.fm stats. | macOS 桌面歌词：逐字同步 · 翻译 · 粤拼 · LyricsX 替代

projects.summary: 一个常驻 macOS 菜单栏的桌面歌词工具。它同时向九个歌词源发起查询，把所有候选放在同一套标准下打分后再决定用哪份，避免现场版配上录音室歌词、粤语版配上国语歌词这类错配。除 Apple Music、Spotify 外，也能读取 QQ 音乐、网易云音乐、酷狗，以及浏览器里播放的网页版音乐。 亮点 歌词智能匹配，而且过程可查：九个源（网易云、QQ 音乐、酷狗、酷我、咪咕、Musixmatch、LRCLIB、LyricFind、AMLL）的全部候选统一打分——歌名/歌手/专辑吻合度、源上报时长与实际曲长的差、有没有逐字时间轴，Live/Remix/(Edit) 这类版本标记单独计分。每首歌都能点开看各候选得了多少分、赢家为什么赢，手动选定的会被锁定不被覆盖。同类项目多是「哪个源先返回就用哪个」。 国产播放器是一等公民：QQ 音乐、网易云、酷狗与 Apple Music、Spotify 同等支持，可多选；浏览器里的网页版音乐也能按页面进度条同步。 支持中文翻译、粤语粤拼、日语注音假名；翻译默认走 macOS 设备端翻译，歌词不出本机。 支持 Last.fm 记录播放，带本地听歌统计、榜单和全年热力图；没连账号也先记在本地，之后连上自动补传。 四种显示形态任意组合：桌面悬浮窗、贴着刘海的灵动岛胶囊、菜单栏歌词（可双排）、仿 Apple Music 的独立歌词窗口。 免费、GPL-3.0、无账号无遥测，Apple Silicon 与 Intel 都有构建。

projects.title: Show HN: Ditch; Build multiple products at once
projects.author: 0xmtn
projects.summary: Hey HN, I built Ditch because I'm running Codex across several projects and was losing track of what each agent was doing, which one needed me, and where I had left off. Plus, I have other work, so I'd like to leave my agents be and come back only when they need me, finish or fail. Ditch is a local desktop app for managing multiple Codex agents simultaneously. It keeps projects and sessions in one place, shows which sessions are active or waiting, notifies you when something needs attention, and makes it easier to move between projects without losing context. I’m also experimenting with remote control, shared context across agents, and higher-level orchestration, but I’m keeping this first release focused on the local Codex workflow in macOS. The Community Edition with its source code is at Github: https://github.com/DitchNow/Ditch I want to keep developing the local runtime as OSS so it can be extended and integrated into workflows beyond what I build into the official app. No account or email required. Just download the dmg and start adding your projects to the app. I’m especially interested in how other HN users organize multiple coding-agent sessions, what causes them to lose context, and which parts of the workflow still feel unnecessarily manual.

projects.title: Show HN: Slock – A one-bit messenger inside your capslock key
projects.author: jonaraphael
projects.summary: Two computers, one bit. Hi — I built slock, a small macOS menu bar app that connects two people through their capslock lights. Hold capslock on your Mac, and the other person’s capslock light turns on. Let go, and it turns off. That’s all. A tiny way to interact someone without opening a chat window. Invent a blink language, try Morse code, or just bother someone who agreed to install this with you. If you both opt in, the same key also becomes a push-to-talk walkie-talkie. It’s open source: simple Swift, end-to-end encrypted, no accounts, no analytics. While it’s running, capslock takes a break from capitalizing things. Pause it to get your old capslock back. Please enjoy this very elaborate way to blink a light. Thank you for checking out my little project!

projects.title: ScanCode
projects.summary: Scan QR codes and barcodes from your screen or camera, see exactly what they contain, and act on them - without leaving your Mac. One keyboard shortcut to scan your screen. Nothing gets uploaded. All processing happens locally. Open payment QR codes directly in your banking app, launch links, or build barcode-based automations.

projects.title: Capturo
projects.summary: A screenshot is a rectangle of pixels cut out of a bigger screen. No edges, no context, which is why one pasted into a slide always looks like it fell there by accident. Capturo fixes that in one pass: padding, background, rounded corners, shadow, window frame and output shape, set together and exported once. Paste straight from the clipboard. Runs in your browser, nothing is uploaded. Plus guides on how screenshots work per platform, in four languages.

projects.title: iWinBridge
projects.summary: iWinBridge moves clipboard text, links, photos, videos and files straight between your iPhone and Windows PC over the same Wi-Fi. Nothing is uploaded and no account is needed. Pair once with a QR code and they reconnect on their own.

projects.title: AutoShortFormVideoGenerator
projects.summary: AutoShortFormVideoGenerator is a desktop tool for turning long videos into short-form content that you can upload to YouTube or TikTok with an automated workflow. Unlike many cloud editing services, it's a one-time purchase. You can also keep your videos private because the program doesn’t require an internet connection, except when it needs to verify your license key. The best thing about the program is that it works for both human streamers and VTubers. Feel free to ask me any questions.

Designed for deep readers, researchers, and writers, it conditions screen light with 8 curated paper stocks, warm tinting, softened ink contrast, and microscopic paper grain. Includes customizable reading sliders, an instant shortcut and runs 100% offline with zero tracking.

projects.title: PDF Unlocker Pro
projects.summary: PDF Unlocker Pro is a secure, 100% offline desktop application for Windows that removes passwords and restrictions from PDF documents locally, keeping confidential files and bank statements completely private.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】Keelhaven：macOS 菜单栏的 restic 备份工具
projects.author: shenxianpeng

github.name: shenxianpeng/keelhaven
github.description: Privacy-first macOS menu-bar backup app powered by restic

projects.summary: Keelhaven 是一个纯菜单栏的 macOS 备份应用，没有 Dock 图标，也没有主窗口。备份引擎是 restic，加密、去重、增量都交给它，Keelhaven 负责界面、定时和密码管理。 用起来是三步：选要保护的文件夹，选一个自己拥有的存储（外置硬盘、NAS/SFTP，或者任意 S3 协议的对象存储，比如 Backblaze B2、Wasabi、Cloudflare R2），再设一个定时（每小时/每天/每周）。设好之后它就在后台安静地跑，只有出错才弹通知。 仓库密码只存在 macOS 钥匙串里，不落盘、不写日志，也不会作为命令行参数传给 restic 子进程。写出来的是标准的 restic 仓库，哪天不用 Keelhaven 了，用 restic 命令行本身也能继续读取和恢复。 restic 需要访问任意目录、网络和 SSH，App Store 的沙盒放不下，所以目前只有 Homebrew 和一行 curl 脚本两种安装方式。还没有申请 Apple 开发者证书：Homebrew 安装会在安装时清掉隔离标记，能直接打开；如果是从网站下载 dmg 双击安装，首次需要手动允许一次。GPLv3 开源，界面支持中英文双语。 brew install --cask shenxianpeng/tap/keelhaven 如果没有 Homebrew 可以通过 curl 命令来安装 curl -fsSL | bash

projects.title: Kairo
projects.summary: Kairo reads any selected text aloud on your Mac from one shortcut, and summarizes, translates or humanizes it on your own OpenAI key.

projects.title: 〖独立工具推荐〗法脉：律师的本地离线法律库 + 法条笔记 + AI 合同审查（macOS）
projects.author: lttxzmj

projects.summary: 我是 SubnetDesk 的作者。SubnetDesk 是一个基于 RustDesk 独立维护的开源远程桌面项目，专门服务于“设备已经网络互通”的场景：同一局域网、可路由私网，或者通过 WireGuard、Tailscale、OpenVPN 等 VPN 连接的网络。 它去掉了公网设备 ID、信令、中继、云账号和代理等路径，改为直接连接 IP 地址或主机名；局域网内还可以通过 mDNS 自动发现设备。比较适合家庭实验室、办公室、教室和现场运维，希望把远程控制链路留在现有私有网络中的用户。 主要特点： 直接连接 IP 地址或主机名，TCP 端口可配置 mDNS 自动发现局域网设备，也支持手动输入地址 用户名和密码认证，密码以 Argon2id 哈希保存 首次连接核对并保存设备指纹，并支持 CIDR 来源网段白名单 保留远程控制、剪贴板、音频和文件传输等 RustDesk 核心体验 提供 Windows、macOS、Linux 和 Android 安装包 当前稳定版是 v1.3.0，采用 AGPL-3.0 许可证。需要说明的是，它不提供公网信令或中继能力，两台设备必须已经可以通过 LAN、私网路由或 VPN 互相访问。
